title: Go engineering
summary: Write and review idiomatic Go that preserves package boundaries, handles every error, propagates context and stays within the approved design.

provenance.notes: Rewritten around the checks a small bounded worker can follow reliably; stylistic advice that gofmt already enforces is omitted.

inputs.name: acceptance
inputs.description: The behavior that must hold when the change is done.

outputs.name: change
outputs.description: A minimal diff inside the allowed files.

outputs.name: notes
outputs.description: Any boundary, error or concurrency concern found while working.

workflow.step: Read the target file, its package's other files and the nearest tests before changing anything.
workflow.check: The change matches the package's existing naming and error style.

workflow.step: Make the smallest change that satisfies the acceptance criteria; keep exported signatures stable unless the task says otherwise.
workflow.check: No unrelated reformatting or renames appear in the diff.

workflow.step: Return errors instead of panicking; wrap with %w and add context that names the operation. Never discard an error with the blank identifier unless a comment states why.
workflow.check: Every call that returns an error is handled.

workflow.step: Pass context.Context as the first parameter of anything that blocks or performs I/O, honor cancellation, and never store a context in a struct.
workflow.check: A cancelled context stops the work.

workflow.step: For goroutines and channels, name the owner that closes the channel and the condition that ends each goroutine.
workflow.check: There is no goroutine without a defined exit.

workflow.step: Run gofmt and the approved targeted go test; fix failures in the code, not in the tests.

constraints: Do not edit test files or add dependencies unless the task explicitly allows it.
Do not introduce global mutable state or init-time side effects.
Stay within the allowed files; report needed changes elsewhere instead of making them.

examples.title: Swallowed error
examples.situation: A helper ignores the error from a close call.
examples.guidance: Return it (or log it with the operation named) and add a test that forces the failure.

verification: gofmt reports no diff and the targeted go test passes.
No new exported API, dependency or goroutine was added beyond what the acceptance criteria require.

task.text: Add context cancellation and error wrapping to this goroutine worker in the package.
Review the golang interface and struct changes for channel leaks.
Add context cancellation and error wrapping to this goroutine worker.
